question: Which of the following is the correct set of raw materials for washing soda preparation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **NaCl, NH₃, and CO₂** are the correct set of raw materials for washing soda preparation.
 
• Washing soda, or sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃), is prepared using the **Solvay process.**
 
• In the Solvay process, **ammonia (NH₃), carbon dioxide (CO₂), and sodium chloride (NaCl)** are the primary raw materials.
 
• These materials react in a series of steps to produce sodium carbonate (washing soda) and other by-products.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the Solvay process, **ammonia** is recovered and recycled, making the process economical.
 
• The process involves several steps including the formation of ammonium bicarbonate, which then reacts with sodium chloride to form sodium bicarbonate and ammonium chloride.
 
• Sodium bicarbonate is then heated to form sodium carbonate (washing soda) and carbon dioxide, which is recycled back into the process.
 
• The Solvay process is widely used in industrial applications due to its efficiency and cost-effectiveness.
